source_text: Ego enim hoc contentus sum, quod mihi es tu dare compulsus, quia, quod praedicavit Apostolus in liberalitate gratiae non possit cunctis aequaliter aetatibus convenire; tu si quid attuleris, quod et in prima nascentium aetate remissionem confirmes exsequi, illud tamen non admovisti, quia non compleatur in parvulis, unde Apostolus gratiam Christi pronuntiavit esse laudabilem. Nam cum medicinam mysterii peccato primi hominis, quem formam fuisse docebat sequentibus, anteferret, ait: Iudicium ex uno delicto in condemnationem, gratia autem ex multis delictis in iustificationem [n166] . Illud ergo, per quod praetulit gratiam, quia ex multis videlicet delictis iustificationem operatur, nec secundum te constat in parvulis; atque ad hoc, quamvis reluctareris, attractus es, ut non aequaliter in diversis aetatibus gratiam faterere versari.
pass_a_gloss: For I am content with this, which you have been compelled to give me, because what the Apostle preached in the liberality of grace cannot fit all ages equally; if you shall have brought anything by which you confirm that remission follows even in the first age of those being born, you have nevertheless not moved this, that that is not completed in little children from which the Apostle pronounced the grace of Christ to be praiseworthy. For when he preferred the medicine of the mystery to the sin of the first human being, whom he was teaching to have been a form to those following, he says: Judgment from one offense into condemnation, but grace from many offenses into justification. That therefore through which he preferred grace, because namely it works justification from many offenses, does not even according to you stand in little children; and to this, although you would struggle, you have been drawn, so that you confessed that grace is not turned equally in diverse ages.

LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system

LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: I am content with what you have been compelled to grant me: what the apostle praised in grace’s generosity cannot apply equally to every age. Even if you adduce something to establish that grace also effects forgiveness at the earliest age of newborn children, you have not altered this: the feature for which the apostle declared Christ’s grace praiseworthy is not fulfilled in infants. For when he ranked the sacrament’s medicine above the sin of the first man, whom he taught was a model for those who followed, he said: ‘The judgment was from one offense to condemnation, but grace is from many offenses to justification’ (Romans 5:16). Therefore the feature by which he ranked grace higher—its producing justification from many offenses—does not hold for infants even according to you. Despite your resistance, you have been brought to acknowledge that grace does not act identically in different ages.

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
